title: $250K, $450K or $1 Million: What Your Money Buys in San Antonio in 2026

description: Where every budget lands in San Antonio in 2026: the neighborhoods and suburbs at $250,000, $450,000 and $1 million, with typical values and yearly property taxes.
keywords: what can I afford in San Antonio

intro: The same budget buys a very different life depending on where you land in Greater San Antonio. Here are the three budgets people ask about most, and exactly where each one fits.

after: Above $832,750, most buyers move from a conforming loan to a jumbo loan, which has different down payment and credit rules. Plan for it early.
Typical home values are the Zillow Home Value Index for August 2026, not sale prices. A specific home can sell well above or below its area's typical value.

sections.h2: What property taxes look like at each budget
paras: Texas has no state income tax, so property taxes do the heavy lifting. Inside the City of San Antonio, combined 2025 rates run about:
items: Northside ISD area: about 2.29% of value a year
New Braunfels in Comal ISD: about 1.79%
after: On a $250,000 home in Northside ISD, that's roughly $5,700 a year before exemptions. Your homestead exemption takes $140,000 off the value for school taxes, which lowers the bill.

faq.q: How much do I need to buy a house in San Antonio?
faq.a: The metro median sale price was $302,999 in September 2026. Several San Antonio ZIP codes and suburbs have typical values under $250,000.

faq.q: What San Antonio neighborhoods cost about $1 million?
faq.a: Hill Country Village, The Dominion, Shavano Park, Terrell Hills and Olmos Park all had typical home values around or above $900,000 in August 2026.

faq.q: What is the property tax rate in San Antonio?
faq.a: Combined 2025 rates inside the city run roughly 2.27% to 2.44% of value a year before exemptions, depending on the school district.
